title: Understanding PCA and SVD
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It involves the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of a centered matrix.

title: Matrix Centering
text: Centering a matrix involves subtracting the mean of each column from the respective column values. This ensures that each column has a mean of zero.

title: SVD Components
text: The SVD of a matrix X is given by X=U*Sigma*V**T, where U and V are orthogonal matrices, and Sigma is a diagonal matrix containing singular values.

title: Interpreting U*Sigma
text: The product U*Sigma represents the projection of the original data onto the principal component space. The first two columns of U*Sigma correspond to the first two principal components.
